description: We are a closed team of friends participating in NASA Space Apps. We are passionate about game development and space technology. Our team already has all the necessary skills (developers and designers). We are not looking for new members, but we are excited to build our project!
summary:
Lunar Relay is a first-person educational game that puts young explorers in charge of a lunar outpost. Built in Unity for Windows and Android, it turns astronaut mission training into a hands-on experience.

Players restore air cleaning, balance electrical power, and prepare a shelter for their crew. They use tools, replace cartridges, service solar equipment, and manage limited resources. These tasks demonstrate how air, water, energy, and crew safety depend on one another.

The project addresses the challenge by making scientific concepts understandable through exploration, practical tasks, and visible consequences. A structured training shift introduces the main responsibilities, while an endless mode supports continued practice.

Lunar Relay aims to spark interest in space exploration and help learners develop problem-solving skills, systems thinking, and an appreciation of the engineering behind living beyond Earth.
details:
Lunar Relay - Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Lunar Relay is a first-person educational game about operating a future lunar outpost. It introduces young learners to the engineering decisions behind living beyond Earth through exploration, practical tasks, and resource management.

How it works

Players have three main responsibilities: restore air cleaning, maintain electrical power, and prepare a crew shelter. They inspect equipment, isolate power before repairs, replace cartridges, use tools, service solar equipment, and transport supplies.

The game connects these actions through a shared simulation. Electrical loads affect battery reserves; air cleaning requires power; oxygen generation consumes water and electricity; and water placed in shelter blocks becomes unavailable for other uses. Players can observe how their decisions affect the base.

A structured shift introduces the main responsibilities, while an endless mode provides recurring tasks and continued practice. Yellow outlines identify interaction targets, and a backpack allows players to carry several items. Completing tasks earns Lunar Credits, which can be spent on decorations that players place inside their base.

Educational value and intended impact

The project makes abstract scientific concepts tangible. Instead of only reading about life-support systems, learners operate them and observe the consequences. The intended impact is to encourage curiosity about space, systems thinking, resource awareness, and practical problem-solving.

Scientific explanations draw on NASA references covering life support, lunar conditions, and shelter design. Accelerated time, equipment ratings, and scripted events are learning assumptions rather than measurements of an actual lunar mission.

Tools and development

The game was developed in Unity using C#, the Universal Render Pipeline, and Unity’s Input System. Python scripts and procedural geometry were used to create and process models and textures. A separate download website uses Flask, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and is hosted on PythonAnywhere. Source code and the seven-slide presentation are publicly available on GitHub.

AI-assisted coding supported development. Automated checks were used to assess simulation behavior, gameplay interactions, saving, purchases, and synthetic touch input. Further testing on physical Android devices remains a development priority.

Creativity and design considerations

Lunar Relay combines scientific resource management with hands-on maintenance and personal base customization. We considered clear objectives, readable interfaces, English and Russian localization, touch controls, different screen sizes, performance, and the balance between scientific explanation and enjoyable play.
